messages:
anya.docs: FYI team — we're deprecating the blocking sync client APIs across first-party SDKs. Reason: streaming + structured responses give better latency and observability. Migration guide: https://redwood.inference/internal/docs/sync-client-deprecation :loud_sound:

jasper.sdk: Oof — timeline? will we remove methods immediately?

anya.docs: Plan: deprecation announcement today, SDKs emit a warn() when sync calls are used starting 2026-04-10, and sync APIs will be removed in the major release on 2026-08-01.

mike.eng: Impact on internal services that embed SDKs synchronously? We have some small microservices using sync wrapper.

tara.product: We'll offer a compatibility shim for one minor release that adapts sync calls to streaming under the hood (with a warning). Customers should move to async/streaming patterns.

jasper.sdk: Which SDKs get the shim? Node and Python first?

anya.docs: Node (all maintained LTS branches) and Python (3.8+) will include the shim and warning for two minor releases. Go and Rust will provide clear migration helpers in the docs instead of a shim.

mike.eng: I'll inventory internal repos and flag callers. Can we add a Console metric to show sync-call % so Support can track customer exposure?

notice-bot: created internal doc page: /internal/docs/sync-client-deprecation and scheduled public KB for 2026-04-11 :calendar:

tara.product: Support/Growth — please draft customer-facing email and a KB snippet. I'll review copy this afternoon.

anya.docs: Thanks — adding a small snippet for migration examples (sync -> async) and a sample shim code block in the guide. Ping me if you need wording for release notes. :thumbsup:
